part.text: All 13 tests pass. Let me also run the linter to make sure the code matches the project's style rules.

Done — all 13 tests in `react.spec.js` pass and the code lints cleanly. The implementation lives entirely in `react.js`:

- **`InputCell`** — holds a `value` and a set of dependent cells. `setValue` updates the value and kicks off propagation (skipping the work entirely if the value didn't change).
- **`ComputeCell`** — computes its value from its input cells at construction, registers itself as a dependent of each input, and keeps a `Set` of callbacks. `addCallback`/`removeCallback` are idempotent set operations, so removing a callback multiple times is harmless.
- **`CallbackCell`** — stores the callback function and a `values` array; its `fire(cell)` method records `fn(cell)`.
- **`propagate(source)`** — a two-phase update: it first collects every cell that transitively depends on the changed input, then recomputes them in true topological order using Kahn's algorithm (each cell is processed only after all of its affected inputs have been recomputed). A cell's callbacks fire only when its value in the new stable state differs from the previous one.

Two subtleties the tests exercise, both handled: callbacks fire exactly once even when a cell has multiple changed dependencies at different depths (the topological ordering guarantees this), and callbacks stay silent when intermediate values change but the output value ends up the same.
